error_message: stitch MCP: 'Failed to connect - Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration'
root_cause: stitch was configured as an http server at https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp. That endpoint requires a pre-registered OAuth client; Claude Code only performs dynamic client registration, so authentication can never succeed. Re-running the OAuth flow cannot fix it.
fix: Replaced with the stdio proxy: claude mcp add stitch -s user -e STITCH_API_KEY=<key> -- npx -y @_davideast/stitch-mcp proxy. The proxy hard-errors without STITCH_API_KEY or STITCH_ACCESS_TOKEN.

error_message: mcp__stitch__download_assets returned 'Assets downloaded to <dir>' but wrote no files anywhere on disk
root_cause: download_assets is a proxy-side convenience tool in @_davideast/stitch-mcp, not a real Stitch API call. It reports success unconditionally and silently writes nothing. Verified by searching the whole filesystem for files modified in the last 15 minutes.
fix: Ignore the tool. Take htmlCode.downloadUrl / screenshot.downloadUrl from list_screens and curl them. The html download URL is a base64 protobuf in which only the html_<32hex> file id varies, so every screen's URL is reconstructable from a constant prefix+suffix; the URLs need no auth.

error_message: e: Cannot access 'androidx.room3.RoomDatabase' which is a supertype of 'AnfasDatabase'. Check your module classpath for missing or conflicting dependencies.
root_cause: :core:database declared `implementation(libs.bundles.room)`, but AnfasDatabase extends RoomDatabase and DatabaseBuilderFactory returns RoomDatabase.Builder — room3-runtime is part of the module's ABI, so a consumer (:core:data) could not compile against it.
fix: Split the bundle: `api(libs.androidx.room3.runtime)` because it is in the ABI, `implementation(libs.androidx.sqlite.bundled)` because the driver is internal to buildDatabase(). Features still never see Room — anfas.kmp.feature withholds :core:database.

error_message: e: Name contains illegal characters: ",". (core/data + feature/members commonTest, only on compileTestKotlinIosSimulatorArm64)
root_cause: Backtick-quoted test function names containing a comma. The JVM target accepts them, so `:core:data:jvmTest` passed and the failure only appeared when `check` reached the Kotlin/Native test compilation.
fix: Stripped , ; : . from all backticked test names. Lesson: run `./gradlew check` (which compiles native test targets) before believing a KMP test suite is green — a jvmTest pass proves nothing about iOS.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference 'number' (kotlinx.datetime.Month.number)
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime 0.8.0's Month has no `number` property.
fix: Index a MonthAbbreviations array by Enum.ordinal; the enum is declared January..December in order.

error_message: e: Overload resolution ambiguity / Conflicting overloads in OfflineFirstMemberRepository.kt (runStorage, asStorageError)
root_cause: Extracted the shared error-boundary helpers into StorageBoundary.kt as `internal` while OfflineFirstMemberRepository.kt still had its own `private` copies with the same names in the same package.
fix: Deleted the private copies and rewrote the member repository to use the shared runStorage/asAppResult. Extracting a helper means removing the original, not adding a second.

error_message: e: Cannot access class 'kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate'. Check your module classpath (from :core:data)
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime was `implementation` in :core:model, but SubscriptionTerm.startsOn and RenewalQuote.endsOn expose LocalDate, so it is part of the module's ABI. Same class of mistake as bug-003 with room3.
fix: Changed to `api(libs.kotlinx.datetime)`. Rule: if a type from a dependency appears in your public signatures, it is `api`.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference 'datetime' in core/common/RelativeTime.kt — only during :core:common:compileCommonMainKotlinMetadata
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime was reached transitively via api(project(":core:model")). Platform compilations (jvmTest) resolved it, but commonMain *metadata* compilation did not, so `:core:common:jvmTest` passed while `check` failed later.
fix: Declared api(libs.kotlinx.datetime) directly in :core:common. Do not rely on a transitive api dependency in commonMain metadata compilation; declare ABI deps explicitly.

error_message: app.cash.turbine.TurbineAssertionError: Unconsumed events found (3 ReminderQueueComponentTest failures)
root_cause: A StateFlow keeps emitting after the assertion of interest — combine() re-emits when any upstream changes. Turbine treats leftover emissions at the end of a test() block as a failure.
fix: End each state.test { } block with cancelAndIgnoreRemainingEvents() once the interesting emission has been asserted.

error_message: e: Unresolved reference. None of the following candidates is applicable because of a receiver type mismatch (clock.now().todayIn(zone))
root_cause: kotlinx-datetime's todayIn is an extension on Clock, not on Instant.
fix: Call clock.todayIn(timeZone) directly.

error_message: Missing error handling in unknown
root_cause: Code path had no error handling — exceptions would propagate uncaught
fix: Added try/catch block

error_message: Null/undefined access in
root_cause: Property access on potentially null/undefined value
fix: Added null safety (optional chaining or null check)

fix: Rewrote 11→6 lines (6 removed) | Also: /** Sentinel for "no particular batch"; the query ; const val BATCH_ANY = ""

error_message: Wrong reference: AppError should be AppResult
root_cause: Used "AppError" instead of "AppResult"
fix: Changed AppError → AppResult

root_cause: 28 lines replaced/restructured

root_cause: Used "width" instead of "size"
fix: Changed width → size

error_message: AssertionError: expected:<[#88393, #88394]> but was:<[#88394]> — only one member imported instead of two
root_cause: The test fixture's newId lambda returned a constant string, so every imported row got the same member primary key and the Room upsert collapsed them into a single row. The repository was correct; the double-checked assertion caught the fixture.
fix: Made the fixture's newId a counter. Lesson: any injected id generator in a test must be unique per call, or upserts silently merge records and the test looks like a product bug.

error_message: e: Conflicting import: imported name 'IntakeReviewComponent' is ambiguous (RootComponent.kt)
root_cause: A python str.replace patch inserted the same import block twice because the anchor line appeared more than once in the file after an earlier partial edit.
fix: Deduplicated the imports by hand. When patching source with replace(), pass a count or assert the anchor occurs exactly once first.

error_message: Significant refactor of
root_cause: 2 lines replaced/restructured
fix: Rewrote 3→42 lines (2 removed)

error_message: Missing error handling in unknown
root_cause: Code path had no error handling — exceptions would propagate uncaught
fix: Added try/catch block

error_message: Error resolving plugin [id: 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.serialization', version: '2.4.10'] > already on the classpath with an unknown version
root_cause: Applied the anfas.quality convention plugin at the ROOT project. That puts the convention project's entire runtime classpath -- including the Kotlin plugins -- on the root buildscript classpath, which every subproject inherits. Subprojects then cannot resolve their own plugin versions.
fix: Root applies Spotless by version-catalog alias instead, with its own small spotless block for root-level .kts. Modules get formatting via their anfas.* convention plugin. Never apply a convention plugin to the root project of this build.

error_message: Execution failed for task ':feature:announcements:spotlessKotlin' > Could not read path '.../merged_res/androidHostTest/.../values-ne_values-ne.arsc.flat'
root_cause: Spotless had targetExclude("**/build/**"), which forces it to ENUMERATE build intermediates in order to exclude them. AGP deletes merged-resource files mid-build, so the enumeration hit a file that had vanished.
fix: Dropped the targetExclude entirely. target("src/**/*.kt") already cannot match build/, which is a sibling of src/. Scope targets narrowly instead of excluding broadly.

error_message: Configuration cache problems: Task ':verifyIosVersionConfig' cannot serialize Gradle script object references
root_cause: A doLast block referenced a script-level function (renderIosVersionConfig). Task actions are serialized for the configuration cache and cannot capture script objects.
fix: Render the expected text at CONFIGURATION time into a local String and have the task action capture only that. Also: do not declare a generated file as an input of the task that verifies it -- Gradle reports an implicit task dependency. Use outputs.upToDateWhen { false } for a verification task instead.

error_message: androidx.sqlite.SQLiteException: Error code: 1555, UNIQUE constraint failed: room_master_table.id (MigrationV4ToV5Test)
root_cause: The test hand-inserted the schema identity hash into room_master_table, but a Room schema JSON's setupQueries ALREADY contain both the CREATE TABLE and the INSERT OR REPLACE for that row.
fix: Execute the schema's setupQueries verbatim and add no manual insert. Room will not recognise a hand-built database as being at version N without that row, so it must come from exactly one place.

error_message: macOS has no `timeout` command -- a verification run silently never started ('command not found: timeout')
root_cause: Used `timeout 90 ./gradlew ...` to bound a run. GNU coreutils is not present on macOS by default, so the whole pipeline failed and the absence of the expected log file was misread as a code problem.
fix: Background the process and poll for the expected condition with an until-loop, then pkill. Do not assume GNU coreutils on this machine.

error_message: expected:<[01001234567]> but was:<[٠١٠٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧]> -- duplicate phone detection silently failing
root_cause: Char.isDigit() returns TRUE for Arabic-Indic digits (U+0660..U+0669), so filter { it.isDigit() } kept them and the same phone number in Arabic numerals produced a different normalisation key. All 18 existing tests used Latin digits.
fix: Fold Arabic-Indic and Eastern Arabic digits to ASCII BEFORE filtering (TextNormalisation.foldDigitsToAscii). Rule: never use isDigit() as a filter when non-Latin input is possible -- fold first.

error_message: Compose MP 1.11.1 has no public API to override the Resources locale; iOS locale changes need an app relaunch
root_cause: LocalComposeEnvironment is internal and ResourceEnvironment has an internal constructor. On iOS, Locale.current reads NSLocale.preferredLanguages, changeable only via NSUserDefaults AppleLanguages and effective next launch.
fix: Do not use Compose Resources for strings when an in-app language toggle is required. A typed AppStrings interface behind a CompositionLocal makes switching an ordinary recomposition on all platforms, and makes a missing translation a compile error.

error_message: Overlay boxes would jump to mirrored positions over a photograph in Arabic
root_cause: Modifier.offset IS layout-direction aware (it negates x under RTL); absoluteOffset is the direction-agnostic one. The plan initially had this backwards. A photograph is not a mirrored artifact, so mirroring the overlay points staff at the wrong line.
fix: Force LocalLayoutDirection = Ltr on the entire image pane, not absoluteOffset on one call -- that also covers future Alignment/Arrangement/gesture code. Fixed alongside a second bug in the same lines: boxes were sized against the pane rather than the rendered image rect, so letterboxing displaced every box.

error_message: Latin-tuned typography breaks Arabic: tofu glyphs, shattered words, unreadable labels
root_cause: Three separate defects. (1) The bundled IBM Plex Sans has no Arabic glyphs, and FontFamily selects by weight not glyph coverage, so merging faces would not help. (2) The export's letter-spacing breaks the joins between letters in a cursive script. (3) labelCaps is 11sp uppercase, meaningless in a script with no letter case.
fix: Bundle IBM Plex Sans Arabic and BRANCH the family by script; zero letterSpacing for Arabic; grow labelCaps 1sp and drop its tracking; add ~10% lineHeight so ascenders/harakat do not clip.

error_message: Repeated self-inflicted breakage from broad python str.replace on source files
root_cause: Patching Kotlin with str.replace against remembered formatting: Spotless had reformatted the files, so anchors matched partially or matched text that had already been rewritten. Results included a sealed interface spliced into the middle of a data class body and a duplicated @Composable annotation.
fix: For multi-line structural edits, replace by LINE RANGE after grepping the current structure, or rewrite the file. Always re-read after Spotless has run.

error_message: Reminder queue tab labels rendered as a vertical stack of single letters ('F a i l e d'), in both English and Arabic
root_cause: Each tab's 2dp selection indicator used Box(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) inside the per-tab Column. fillMaxWidth resolves against the INCOMING max constraint, not the sibling label's width, so the first tab's Column claimed the entire Row width and every later tab was measured at ~one character wide.
fix: Bound the per-tab Column with Modifier.width(IntrinsicSize.Max) so fillMaxWidth means 'as wide as this tab's label row'. Added maxLines=1/softWrap=false on the label and horizontalScroll on the strip so a future overflow clips or scrolls instead of shattering.

error_message: Language toggle crammed into the bottom navigation bar as a fourth slot; completely absent on the wide/rail layout
root_cause: App.kt passed the toggle as AnfasBottomNav(trailing = toggle), which stole width from three real destinations and crowded the bar's end edge. AnfasNavRail's footer slot existed but was never passed anything, so on desktop/tablet there was no way to change language at all.
fix: Moved the toggle to an end-aligned row above the Host on compact, and passed footer = toggle to AnfasNavRail on wide. A language switch is not a navigation destination.

error_message: Members empty state: 'SCAN SHEET' wrapped onto two lines while the adjacent 'ADD MEMBER' stayed on one
root_cause: The two action buttons sat in a plain Row, so on a phone they competed for width and whichever was measured second wrapped its label at a different height from its neighbour.
fix: Switched the actions container to FlowRow with vertical spacing, so the buttons stack on a narrow screen and stay inline on a wide one.

error_message: checkAndroidHostTestAarMetadata FAILED: Dependency 'androidx.core:core:1.19.0' requires Android Gradle plugin 9.1.0 or higher / compileSdk 37
root_cause: androidx-core was pinned at 1.19.0 in the catalog but had no Android-compiling consumer, so the incompatibility was latent. :core:ocr became the first consumer (FileProvider) and surfaced it. AGP is capped at 9.0.1 by the installed Android Studio.
fix: Downgraded androidx-core to 1.18.0, the highest release compatible with AGP 9.0.1 / compileSdk 36, and added it to CLAUDE.md's version-ceiling table next to androidx-lifecycle.

error_message: Intake review table showed Start, End and Plan as empty for every row, while still reporting '4 of 4 rows ready for import'
root_cause: The Android recogniser emitted ML Kit Text.Line boxes. ML Kit fuses text on a shared baseline when horizontal gaps are small, so 'Nov 1, 2023 Dec 1, 2023Monthly' arrived as ONE box spanning x 0.63..0.99 across three columns. A box spanning three columns cannot be assigned to any of them, so all three cells came out blank -- and the row still counted as importable.
fix: Emit word-level Text.Element boxes instead of Text.Line, falling back to the line when a model reports no elements. Verified on a real emulator scan: 21 boxes became 51, and all six columns populate.

error_message: With word-level OCR input the parser produced empty dates and plan, and appended 'Nov', 'Dec' and '2023Monthly' to the member's NAME
root_cause: IntakeSheetParser classified each incoming box independently. That works for line-level input ('Nov 1, 2023' parses as a date) but not word-level ('Nov' parses as nothing), so every fragment fell through to the unclaimed bucket and anything with letters was swept into the name cell.
fix: Added a mergeIntoCells stage that groups a row's boxes into cells by horizontal gap before any classification, making the parser independent of recogniser granularity. Calibrated Tuning.minColumnGap from 0.03 to 0.015 against measured ML Kit output (word gaps 0.005-0.009, column gaps 0.017+). Also replaced the name-cell guard with a strict no-digits rule so fused debris like '2023Monthly' can never enter a name. Two regression tests added.

error_message: Intake footer's IMPORT button rendered as a featureless amber vertical sliver on a phone
root_cause: The footer Row used Arrangement.SpaceBetween with an unweighted Text. Unweighted children are measured first at their full intrinsic width, so 'N of N rows ready for import' consumed the row and the button group was measured at whatever remained. Same class of defect as the AnfasTabs indicator bug.
fix: Gave the label Modifier.weight(1f) so the buttons are measured at intrinsic size and the label takes the remainder, plus FlowRow so the label stacks above the actions on a narrow screen.

error_message: Every cell in the intake and members tables truncated to a few characters on a phone ('Omar Ha...', 'Activ e', 'ACTIO NS', 'ID:' with no number)
root_cause: Both tables lay out columns with Modifier.weight, which is correct at the desktop widths the design was drawn at. On a ~360dp phone the same weights divide the width between four to six columns and every cell clips. On the intake review screen that hides the OCR misreads the screen exists to surface; on members it hid the membership number entirely, which looked like import failing to assign one.
fix: Added a shared AnfasTableScroll that keeps a 640dp minimum table width and scrolls horizontally below it, wrapping only the header and rows so an action footer stays fixed. Applied to both tables. A fillHeight flag is required because forcing fillMaxHeight consumed the height the members footer needed and pushed 'Showing N members' off screen.

error_message: iOS: white bands above the status bar and below the home indicator, framing a #141311 app
root_cause: ContentView applied .ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard) only, so SwiftUI inset the Compose view by the top and bottom safe areas and the window's own white background showed through. App.kt already applies its own safe padding, so the insets were being handled twice — once in the wrong layer.
fix: Changed to .ignoresSafeArea() with no arguments so Compose owns every edge and paints the background full-bleed. Also set UIUserInterfaceStyle=Dark in Info.plist so the status bar draws light glyphs and system sheets arrive in dark mode.

error_message: Android: full-screen white flash on every cold start before the dark app appeared
root_cause: The launch window used the wizard's @android:style/Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar. That theme only paints the starting window, but that window is the first thing shown on every cold start — white, against a #141311 app.
fix: Added Theme.Anfas (parent Theme.Material.NoActionBar) with windowBackground set to the app background and transparent system bars, and pointed the manifest at it. windowLight*Bar entries were dropped: false is already the default and windowLightNavigationBar needs API 27 against minSdk 24, which fails lint.

error_message: Renewal sheet content was cut off in landscape with no way to scroll to it
root_cause: The root Column had only fillMaxWidth(), so its height was wrap-content. Modifier.weight divides a BOUNDED height, so the weighted child fell back to its intrinsic height, verticalScroll measured its content unbounded, and the column grew taller than the window — the scroll never engaged. In portrait the content happened to fit, which is why it looked fine.
fix: Root is fillMaxSize() and the scroll region uses weight(1f) with fill=true, which bounds the viewport and pins the action footer below it. Verified by rotating a Pixel 9 emulator: the sheet scrolls and Confirm/Cancel stay reachable.

error_message: Bottom navigation had unequal tap targets that moved when the language changed
root_cause: Items were laid out with Arrangement.SpaceEvenly over intrinsically-sized children, so each destination's tap target was sized by its own label — 'Reminders' was visibly larger than 'Intake', and every target shifted between English and Arabic. The selected state also filled the whole cell, so it changed shape per label, and there was no minimum touch target.
fix: Rewrote as equal weight(1f) columns with a 56dp minimum height (clears Material's 48dp and Apple's 44pt), an animated pill indicator behind the icon only, 24dp icons, animated colour transitions, ripple clipped to the cell, and maxLines=1 with ellipsis on the label.

error_message: Table column heading rendered as 'ACTIO / NS', taller than the cells beneath it
root_cause: AnfasTableHeaderCell had no line limit, so a heading narrower than its text wrapped and pushed the header row taller than its own columns.
fix: maxLines = 1 with TextOverflow.Ellipsis — a heading that cannot fit should shorten rather than reflow.

error_message: W ComponentDiscovery: NoSuchMethodException: com.google.mlkit.vision.text.internal.TextRegistrar.<init> [] -- in the R8-minified build only
root_cause: ML Kit registers components through Firebase's ComponentDiscovery, which reads class names out of AndroidManifest meta-data and instantiates them reflectively. R8 sees no caller and strips the no-arg constructors. It surfaces as a WARNING, so nothing crashes -- text recognition just silently never initialises, in release builds only.
fix: -keep class * implements com.google.firebase.components.ComponentRegistrar { <init>(); } -- names as well as constructors, because the manifest refers to these classes by their original fully-qualified names. Verified by installing the minified APK and running a real scan: 51 boxes to 4 rows, identical to debug.

error_message: Gradle script compilation: Unresolved reference 'util'; Return type mismatch: expected 'Properties?', actual 'Unit'
root_cause: Inside a Gradle Kotlin DSL script `java` resolves to the JavaPluginExtension, which shadows the java package, so java.util.Properties cannot be written fully qualified. Separately, Properties().apply { inputStream().use(::load) } returns Unit because use() discards apply's receiver.
fix: Imported Properties (ktlint requires java imports last, and the explanatory comment had to move out of the import block or ktlint refuses to autocorrect) and used .also { props -> file.inputStream().use(props::load) }.

error_message: Member profile: 'Time remaining 0%' with an empty bar on a membership paid the same day
root_cause: The bar was fed TermProgress.fraction, which is the proportion of the term ELAPSED, while the label read 'Time remaining'. On day one of a term that is 0%, so a member who had just paid saw an empty bar.
fix: Added TermProgress.remainingFraction and remainingPercent as their own tested properties, so the semantics live with the calculation rather than at the call site, and displayed the numeric percentage beside the bar because a full or empty bar alone is ambiguous.

error_message: Arabic member profile rendered the date as '22 2026 أغسطس' and the member id as '10003#'
root_cause: Both strings were rendered with the dataMonoLtr style, which forces TextDirection.Ltr. That style is correct for Latin-only data, but these strings CONTAIN Arabic — a translated month name, and the 'رقم العضوية' label — so forcing LTR reordered those runs. Separately, the direction-neutral '#' resolves its direction from its surroundings, so in an RTL paragraph it migrated to the far side of the number.
fix: Added String.asLtrIsolate() using LRI/PDI (U+2066/U+2069) and wrapped only the NUMBER inside the Arabic id string, leaving the label to follow the paragraph. Dates and money now use dataMono rather than dataMonoLtr, since they are localised strings containing script. dataMonoLtr is reserved for Latin-only runs such as phone numbers.

error_message: Denying camera access on iOS did nothing — requestCameraAccess() and openAppSettings() were built in Phase 3 and never called from anywhere
root_cause: The iOS capture path presented UIImagePickerController without first checking authorisation, so a denied camera produced a black picker and no explanation. A repo-wide grep showed both permission APIs had zero callers outside the module that declared them.
fix: onCaptureRequested(launch) checks access before handing control to the screen's launcher, and a denial becomes sticky state showing the camera-denied empty state with an Open Settings action plus the still-valid Choose photo fallback. A `when` guard makes the denial outrank the normal empty state so 'New scan' is never offered while the OS is refusing.

error_message: The CameraAccess.Denied branch was untestable — no test could ever reach it
root_cause: requestCameraAccess() and openAppSettings() were top-level `expect` functions. A top-level expect has no substitution point, so on the JVM test target it always returned NotRequired — meaning the only branch the denial UI exists for could never be exercised.
fix: Introduced a CameraPermissions interface with PlatformCameraPermissions delegating to the expect functions, registered in ocrModule and injected into the component. Same reasoning as AppDispatchers existing rather than reaching for Dispatchers.IO. Three tests now cover denied, granted and open-settings.

error_message: After signing out, the app showed 'Set up this device' instead of the login form, with the previous user's name and username still in the fields
root_cause: The component decided its mode once in init. The shell creates it eagerly at startup — before any account exists — so it latched FirstRun and never re-evaluated. Submitting would have self-healed via AlreadyInitialised, but the user was shown the wrong form. Retaining the fields also left the previous person's details on screen, which matters on a shared reception device.
fix: The component now collects observeSession() and re-runs hasAnyAccount() whenever the session becomes null, replacing the whole state so the form is cleared too. Regression test added.

error_message: MigrationV4ToV5Test FAILED: schema version should now be 5 expected:<5> but was:<6>
root_cause: The test hardcoded the target schema version and was named for it. Adding the staff table for sign-in took the database to v6, so opening a v4 file now migrates all the way forward — the test broke for a reason unconnected to what it verifies.
fix: Renamed to MigrationFromV4Test and generalised: it now asserts the whole chain ran (placeholder dropped by v5, staff added by v6, the member row survived) and that migrating never invents a staff account. The version number moved to a named constant with a note that the assertion which matters is that the chain applied.

error_message: The ADD MEMBER button did nothing
root_cause: onAddMemberClicked was wired to an empty lambda in RootComponent because no add form existed. Both the header button and the empty state's action were dead.
fix: Added a two-field form as component state (so a rotation does not lose a half-typed name) plus MemberRepository.create, which allocates the membership number rather than letting a form invent one. Gated on Permission.EDIT_MEMBERS and hidden rather than disabled for a role that cannot register anybody.

error_message: Start, End and Plan appeared to be missing from the intake review table on a phone, and their inline editors were unreachable
root_cause: A six-column weighted table needs 640dp, so AnfasTableMinWidth made those three columns reachable only by scrolling sideways on a ~366dp phone. The AnfasInlineEditField editors had been wired for every cell all along; they were simply off-screen with the columns.
fix: Narrow screens now render one card per scanned row, every field labelled and editable in place, with Start and End side by side because a wrong end date is only obvious next to its start. The table is kept above AnfasTableMinWidth.

error_message: The validation message in an inline edit field was drawn on top of the value it was complaining about — 'Duplicate' over '01001234567'
root_cause: The value and the error were both children of a Box, which stacks its children. The component's own KDoc said the message goes 'underneath', so this was wrong from the start; the table's narrow cells made the overlap read as clutter rather than as a bug.
fix: Changed the Box to a Column. Found immediately once the intake row cards gave the field full width.

error_message: Membership numbers were allocated by a rule private to the intake repository, so a member added by hand could collide with an imported one
root_cause: nextMembershipNumber() and formatNumber() lived inside OfflineFirstIntakeRepository. The manual add form needed the same rule, and duplicating it would have meant two policies against one unique index.
fix: Extracted MembershipNumbers into :core:model, pure and tested, with a nextRun() that allocates a whole import in one pass. Also fixed a real edge case found while testing: a stray number below FIRST (legacy or hand-typed) used to drag the sequence down, so one member at '#1' meant the next was '#2' rather than '#10000'.

error_message: Adding the members notice made the search field and the ADD MEMBER button disappear
root_cause: The notice was inserted inside the search Row rather than after it, and its fillMaxWidth/weight starved both siblings to zero width. Third occurrence of this exact defect: the AnfasTabs indicator and the intake footer label were the first two.
fix: Moved it out of the Row, with a comment naming the pattern.

error_message: Retry on the reminder queue was not gated on Permission.RETRY_REMINDERS - the tab was, the action was not
root_cause: RBAC enforcement covered routes and the nav bar, but viewing the queue (VIEW_REMINDERS) and re-sending from it (RETRY_REMINDERS) are separate permissions living on the same screen. The route guard cannot distinguish them, so a coach could have re-sent WhatsApp messages on the gym's account.
fix: The session is folded into state as mayRetry; supportsSelection requires it so bulk selection is withheld too, and retry() returns early when it is false - a permission that exists only as a hidden button is not a boundary, because a component method is callable from anywhere. Test asserts the repository is never reached.

error_message: KSP: missing 'JOIN' at 'WHERE'; SQLITE_ERROR near WHERE: syntax error
root_cause: A correlated subquery used `inner` as its table alias. INNER is a SQL keyword, so Room's query verifier parsed it as the beginning of an INNER JOIN.
fix: Renamed the alias to `latest`, with a note in the KDoc so the next person does not repeat it.

error_message: Today's check-in log rendered as a 12-pixel sliver showing one clipped row
root_cause: The log card was the last child of a non-scrolling Column with no weight, so after the header, three summary figures and the search field it received whatever vertical space was left - almost none. Found via a uiautomator dump showing the row's bounds as 12px tall.
fix: The log card takes weight(1f) and its LazyColumn fills it, same pattern as the members table. Both entries then rendered with their outcome chips.

error_message: adb exec-out screencap returned entirely black frames while the app was rendering correctly
root_cause: The emulator's capture surface broke after a long session of installs and rotations. Not an app fault: a uiautomator dump showed 59 nodes with all the expected text, and logcat showed no exception.
fix: Verify via `uiautomator dump` and read the semantics tree instead - it is stronger evidence than a screenshot anyway, since it proves the accessibility tree rather than pixels. Do not conclude 'blank screen means broken app' without checking the node tree first.

error_message: Six routes in the bottom navigation bar; every label ellipsised in Arabic on a narrow phone
root_cause: Every new feature was added to TopLevel as a matter of course. The bar divides the width equally between its items, so six items on a 448dp screen gave each about 74dp - less than an Arabic label needs. Material caps a bottom bar at five and iOS at five-plus-More for exactly this reason.
fix: Reduced TopLevel to four by asking which entries are *places* rather than by dropping the least important. Intake is a task whose product is members, so it became an action in the members header and is pushed - back returns to the directory the new rows joined. Staff management is administration, so it moved to the top bar's overflow menu beside language and sign out. Both remain real permission-guarded routes; only the entry point moved. Added a test asserting no role is offered more than four destinations.

error_message: Members table footer read 'Showing 5 members' in English underneath an otherwise fully Arabic screen
root_cause: The footer built the sentence inline with an if/else on count instead of calling s.members.showingMembers(count). The i18n key and its six Arabic plural forms existed all along - this one call site simply never used them, so the string sweep that externalised the rest of the screen missed it.
fix: Call strings.members.showingMembers(members.size). Found by reading a uiautomator dump of the Arabic build and noticing one Latin string among the Arabic ones - a compile-time-complete string interface cannot catch a key that is never called, so only running the app in the other language finds these.

error_message: Chrome edges (bottom bar top, header underside) drawn with the table rule alpha, half as visible as the export specifies
root_cause: AnfasTableDivider was reused for chrome because it was the only horizontal rule in the design system. The export draws rules between table rows at white/5 and chrome edges at white/10 - two different tokens - so the bar stopped reading as a surface of its own and the content appeared to run into it.
fix: Added AnfasEdgeDivider at AnfasTheme.alphas.border (10%) with a KDoc saying the two are not interchangeable, and used it on AnfasBottomNav, AnfasDetailTopBar and the compact top bar. The rail's vertical divider already used the border alpha and was already correct.

error_message: Back button on the intake screen did nothing when the screen was reached from the desktop rail
root_cause: Intake is pushed from the members header on a phone but selected as a rail destination on desktop, and a rail selection is replaceAll. So on desktop the stack held one entry and Decompose's pop() silently did nothing - the AnfasDetailTopBar back arrow was dead, and desktop has no system back gesture to fall back on.
fix: popOrGoTo(fallback): pop when the back stack is non-empty, otherwise onTopLevelSelected(fallback). Intake falls back to Members, staff to Dashboard. Same shape as the existing onPermissionDeniedDismissed. A screen reachable both by push and by rail selection must never use a bare pop().

error_message: The classes week grid never appeared on an iPad Pro 13 - the day-view list showed instead, even in landscape
root_cause: The grid's compact/wide switch compared BoxWithConstraints width against AnfasBreakpoints.tabletMax (1024dp), which is the constant that decides rail-vs-bottom-bar for the whole app shell. That constant is measured against the window; a screen hosted inside the shell only ever receives window-minus-256dp (the rail's width). So the grid needed a window over ~1280dp to ever appear, which no iPad in this app's supported range reaches.
fix: Derived GRID_MIN_WIDTH from what the grid actually needs to draw - the hour axis plus seven columns wide enough for a class name, coach and capacity (56dp + 7*100dp) - and compared local maxWidth against that instead of the shell's breakpoint. Documented in the constant's KDoc so the mistake is explained, not just fixed.

error_message: The Arabic week grid showed the literal text '$count مكانًا' under every class block instead of the actual capacity number
root_cause: The new Classes strings were written using Kotlin's escaped ${'$'} form (to keep '$' literal text inside a raw string elsewhere in the file), but that escape was carried into places that needed real interpolation. ${'$'}count in Kotlin produces the LITERAL text "$count", not the value of the variable - it compiles cleanly and no existing test caught it because nothing asserted the rendered CONTENT of a translated string, only that the interface was implemented.
fix: Replaced every ${'$'}param with plain $param (9 occurrences: places, emptyDayTitle, durationMinutes, roomClash, saved, deleted). Added PlaceholderInterpolationTest in :core:i18n that renders every Classes string in both languages and asserts (a) no '$' survives into the output and (b) the given argument actually appears in the result - a permanent regression guard, since only running the built UI in the target language would otherwise catch this.

error_message: A pain-score trend phrased as "$first → $latest" would have read backwards in Arabic RTL
root_cause: A directional arrow glyph inside bidi text does not reorder with the surrounding paragraph the way the two numbers around it do. In an RTL context the visual result reads as latest-then-first even though the string was authored first-then-latest, the same class of bug documented in bug-062's ancestor issue with the check-in progress bar and with icon autoMirror -- but here it was a text arrow, not a widget property, so there is no autoMirror equivalent to reach for.
fix: Rewrote the trend as real words instead of a symbol: "$first to $latest" in English, "من $first إلى $latest" ("from X to Y") in Arabic. Word order in a real sentence follows the language's own grammar and sidesteps the directional-glyph question entirely. Caught by reasoning about RTL semantics before writing device-test seed data, then confirmed correct on an iPad simulator: renders as من 5 إلى 3.

error_message: Editing an already-published announcement showed both 'Delete draft' and 'Publish' in the form footer
root_cause: The footer's action list was written for the draft case only and never checked AnnouncementForm.wasPublished before showing Delete/Publish; the component's onRequestPublish() had no guard either, so even bypassing the UI could re-publish and silently overwrite the frozen publishedAt/recipientCountAtPublish (there is no unpublish by design). Found via on-device testing on the iPad Pro 13" simulator, not by unit tests -- this was purely a UI-composition-layer omission with no test covering the footer's button set.
fix: Rewrote AnnouncementFormDialog's footer to branch exclusively on form.wasPublished: draft shows Delete+Cancel+SaveDraft+Publish, published shows only Cancel+SaveChanges (as the primary button, added a new saveChanges i18n string). Also added a defensive `if (form.wasPublished) return` guard directly inside AnnouncementsComponent.onRequestPublish(), consistent with the codebase's rule that a component method must enforce its own invariants since it is callable from anywhere, not just from the dialog that currently withholds the button. Added AnnouncementsComponentTest.kt's 'onRequestPublish is a no-op for an already-published announcement' as the regression test.

error_message: e: ...EquipmentComponentTest.kt:95:9 Name contains illegal characters: ",".
root_cause: Kotlin/Native mangles a backtick-quoted test function name into a symbol name, and a comma in that name produces an illegal Kotlin/Native symbol. Only compileTestKotlinIosSimulatorArm64 catches this -- jvmTest and the JVM compile both pass silently, so it is invisible unless the iOS test target is actually built. This is a recurrence of a previously-logged gotcha (see related_bugs) rediscovered because the earlier lesson wasn't checked before naming a new test.
fix: Renamed the test from 'search matches name or asset tag, case-insensitively' to 'search matches name or asset tag case-insensitively' (dropped the comma, keeping the meaning).

error_message: The photographed sign-up sheet was not visible at all on a phone: intake's source pane was omitted below 1024dp
root_cause: ReviewBody's narrow branch rendered only ValidationPane, inside a Column with verticalArrangement=spacedBy(16.dp) wrapping a single child -- a vestigial container showing the intent was two stacked panes. The screen KDoc said 'the split becomes stacked below 1024dp', which is not what the code did. Net effect: the source photo was unreachable on a phone, the very device that captures it, so the photo-rendering feature shipped one commit earlier was invisible on Android and iPhone.
fix: Added SourceDocumentPane to the narrow branch above ValidationPane using the same SOURCE_PANE_WEIGHT/TABLE_PANE_WEIGHT 40/60 split, vertically; corrected the KDoc to describe what it now does and why dropping the photo was worse than a small zoomable pane. Verified on the Pixel 9 Pro emulator: the sheet renders correctly oriented with overlay boxes aligned.

error_message: The desktop app opened on the mobile bottom-bar layout, making Announcements and Equipment unreachable on desktop
root_cause: Window() was created with no state and no minimum size, so it used Compose's 800x600 default -- below AnfasBreakpoints.tabletMax (1024dp), the point where App.kt switches to the phone layout. The phone layout's bottom bar carries only the four Placement.Primary destinations, so both Placement.DesktopOnly features (Announcements, Equipment) had no entry point at all in the desktop app unless the user manually dragged the window wider.
fix: rememberWindowState(width=1280.dp, height=840.dp) plus an AWT window.minimumSize of 1060x680 set in a LaunchedEffect (Compose's Window has no minimumSize parameter). Past the breakpoint rather than exactly on it so chrome/rounding cannot land back on the phone layout. Confirmed by relaunching: the full rail with Announcements and Equipment Inventory now renders.

error_message: CI: Undefined symbols for architecture arm64: _OBJC_CLASS_$_UIViewLayoutRegion, referenced from CMPLayoutRegion.o; framework 'UIUtilities' not found
root_cause: Both macOS jobs ran on the macos-15 runner image, whose Xcode is 16.4. Compose Multiplatform 1.11.1's UIKit layer references iOS 26 SDK symbols, so Kotlin/Native linking of the test binary and the release framework fails there. Local development is on Xcode 26.6 with the iOS 26.5 SDK, which is why the workflow's commands passed locally and failed only on the runner -- the failure was invisible until the first real CI run.
fix: Moved the `apple` and `ios-app` jobs to runs-on: macos-26, and added a step to both that selects the newest installed Xcode and prints `xcodebuild -version` (plus the simulator SDK list on the apple job), so a future runner-image regression surfaces as one readable line instead of hundreds of linker errors.

error_message: User report: 'the add class button on simulator iphone not properly rendered' -- the Classes title ran flush into the Add class button with no gap, reading as clipped text
root_cause: AnfasScreenHeader's Row used Arrangement.SpaceBetween with the title Column taking Modifier.weight(1f, fill = false). SpaceBetween can only distribute space that is left OVER, and a weight(1f) child claims the entire remaining share -- so once the title is long enough to fill that share there is no space left to distribute and the title lands flush against the first action, with zero separation. It only showed on the narrower iPhone (~402dp): on the Pixel (~427dp) 'Today's schedule' had just enough room that the absence of a gutter was not obvious. Not a clipping bug -- the glyphs were complete, there was simply no gap, which reads as clipping.
fix: Gave the actions Row a Modifier.padding(start = 16.dp) gutter. Padding rather than an Arrangement gap on purpose: it becomes part of the actions' MEASURED width, which is what shrinks the title's weighted share, so an over-long title now wraps instead of colliding. Verified on iPhone 17 (title wraps to two lines, clear space around the button), on the Pixel 9 Pro (still one line, now with breathing room), and on Members, which is the two-action worst case.

error_message: Desktop database was written to ~/.anfas on every OS, which is wrong on macOS and Windows
root_cause: create() hardcoded File(System.getProperty("user.home"), ".anfas"). macOS has a standard Application Support directory that Migration Assistant and backup tooling understand; a dot-directory in a Windows profile can end up synced to OneDrive, which for SQLite means a .db being copied out from under an open connection and away from its -wal. The correct per-OS pattern already existed one module over for logs (core/common/.../AppLog.jvm.kt) with injectable params and a unit test -- the database was simply the odd one out.
fix: Added resolveDesktopDataDir(osName, userHome, localAppData, xdgDataHome) mirroring AppLog.desktopLogFile's shape: macOS Library/Application Support/ANFAS, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%/ANFAS, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/anfas (data locations, deliberately not the log ones). Plus adoptLegacyDatabase(from,to): never overwrites an existing newer DB, moves -wal/-shm as a set before the .db so an interrupted move leaves the legacy dir authoritative, and never throws so a permissions problem cannot become a failure to start. 9 tests in DesktopDataDirTest; verified against a real 135KB database which moved with integrity_check clean and the v11 identity hash unchanged.

error_message: Quitting the desktop app abandoned the Room connection: anfas.db-wal/-shm left behind, Decompose lifecycle never torn down
root_cause: onCloseRequest was ::exitApplication only -- no AnfasDatabase.close() and no lifecycle teardown, so the LifecycleRegistry was resume()d and never stopped. SQLite recovers from an uncheckpointed WAL on next open, but a .db copied by a backup tool while the WAL still holds recent commits is an incomplete database.
fix: Declared the close on the Koin definition that opens it -- single<AnfasDatabase> { ... }.withOptions { onClose { it?.close() } } in dataModule -- so no platform launcher has to remember. main.kt now does lifecycle.destroy() then stopKoin() then exitApplication(), in that order, so components cancel their scopes before the connection closes. NOTE: `single { } onClose { }` reads naturally and does NOT compile; in Koin 4.2 onClose is an extension on BeanDefinition reachable only inside withOptions. KoinOnCloseContractTest pins that contract (2 tests) using an isolated koinApplication rather than the global context, because the real dataModule resolves the user's actual data directory.

error_message: .gitignore un-ignored keystore.properties.template, but that file never existed
root_cause: A negation rule (!keystore.properties.template) was added alongside the keystore.properties ignore, following the Local.xcconfig.template precedent, but the template itself was never created -- so anyone cloning the repo had no idea what keys the signing config expects.
fix: Created it with the four keys androidApp/build.gradle.kts actually reads (storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias, keyPassword), the keytool command to generate a keystore, a warning that losing it means never updating the app under the same package, and the apksigner command to verify what signed an APK. Confirmed trackable via `git add --dry-run` while keystore.properties itself stays ignored.

error_message: R8SmokeTest: all 5 instrumented tests failed with NoSuchMethodError / NoClassDefFoundError (BuildersKt.runBlocking, kotlin.collections.CollectionsKt, GlobalContext.getOrNull, DefaultComponentContext.<init>)
root_cause: The tests called library APIs that the production app never calls, so R8 correctly shrank them out of the app APK. Anything a test reaches for from outside is by definition unreachable from the app, so it is absent from a minified build.
fix: Rewrote the suite to drive the app only through its own entry points (ActivityScenario.launch / recreate) and to assert with org.junit.Assert instead of kotlin.test. Dropped all project dependencies and kotlin.test from androidTest.

error_message: AndroidJUnitRunner crashed in onCreate: NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Lkotlin/LazyKt; at androidx.test.platform.io.TestDirCalculator
root_cause: kotlin-stdlib is a dependency of both the app and the androidTest APK, and AGP ships a shared dependency in the app APK only. The app inlines every `lazy` call so retains no kotlin.LazyKt, while androidx.test's own Kotlin code calls it. -dontshrink in testProguardFiles cannot help: stdlib is not the test APK's program input.
fix: New proguard-rules-stage.pro with `-keep class kotlin.LazyKt* { *; }`, applied via proguardFile() on the `stage` build type only so release is untouched. Verified: release's mapping still shows kotlin.LazyKt__LazyKt -> R8$$REMOVED$$CLASS$$766.

error_message: Missing classes detected while running R8: com.google.errorprone.annotations.CanIgnoreReturnValue / MustBeClosed (task :androidApp:minifyStageAndroidTestWithR8)
root_cause: Because `stage` is minified, the androidTest APK is minified too. androidx.test's Checks/Tracer carry ErrorProne annotations that are compile-time only and ship in a module nothing here depends on.
fix: New proguard-rules-test.pro wired via testProguardFiles, holding -dontwarn com.google.errorprone.annotations.** (plus -dontshrink, since the test APK is not the artifact under test). Kept out of proguard-rules.pro so a test dependency never loosens the shipped app's config.

error_message: Could not resolve org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-json:1.11.0 -- constraint {strictly 1.8.0} from stageRuntimeClasspath by consistent resolution
root_cause: AGP applies consistent resolution: an androidTest configuration must resolve the same versions as the production runtime. The Android classpath never declares serialization-json directly, so the transitively-supplied kotlinx BOM pins everything to 1.8.0, and the catalog's 1.11.0 is excluded by the strict constraint.
fix: Removed the androidTestImplementation declaration entirely and redesigned the test not to need serialization-json (ActivityScenario.recreate exercises the serializers through the app instead).

error_message: Desktop window geometry was never persisted: the com/anfas/app preferences node stayed empty after running the app
root_cause: The save path read WindowState.position, which stays WindowPosition.PlatformDefault when the platform is what placed the window -- the first-run case. toGeometry() therefore returned null for every emission and filterNotNull dropped them all.
fix: Read geometry from the AWT frame (window.x/y/width/height) inside FrameWindowScope, driven by a ComponentAdapter for moves/resizes plus one direct read for the initial placement (which fires no event). Also removes the dp-vs-px unit mismatch, since AWT bounds and GraphicsConfiguration bounds share one space.

error_message: Misdiagnosed 'the preferences write is not happening' -- defaults read and plistlib both showed no window.* keys while they were in fact written
root_cause: macOS cfprefsd serves a cached copy of com.apple.java.util.prefs.plist, so keys written seconds earlier read as absent from both `defaults read` and a direct plistlib load of the file.
fix: Verify java.util.prefs from a fresh JVM instead: Preferences.userRoot().node("com/anfas/app").keys(). That showed all five window.* keys present.

error_message: WindowGeometryTest > a window hanging off the right edge keeps a grabbable strip on screen FAILED
root_cause: The overlap gate and the position clamp used the same constant (MIN_VISIBLE_WIDTH), so anything with less than that visible was rejected before the clamp could run -- making the clamp dead code and recentring a window a user had deliberately parked off an edge.
fix: Weakened the gate to 'any overlap at all' (the detached-monitor case) and left the clamp to guarantee the grabbable minimum. A window parked off an edge is now nudged back into reach rather than recentred.

error_message: User: 'when entering in the input texts in signin and signup the screen not responsive with the keyboard the input components shown under the keyboard'
root_cause: MainActivity calls enableEdgeToEdge() but the activity declared no windowSoftInputMode, so the system used adjustPan: the whole window slid up by a fixed amount instead of the IME being reported as an inset. The ANFAS top bar was pushed under the status bar and whether a field cleared the keyboard depended on the pan distance.
fix: Added android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize" to the MainActivity declaration, with a comment explaining that edge-to-edge requires it.

error_message: Focused text field remained two-thirds under the keyboard on a landscape phone even with a correctly inset scroll container
root_cause: Compose brings a newly-focused field into view at the moment focus arrives, when the keyboard is not yet open and the field is usually already visible, so nothing scrolls. The viewport then shrinks by the keyboard height and no second bring-into-view is issued.
fix: AnfasTextField now holds a BringIntoViewRequester with a LaunchedEffect keyed on both `focused` and WindowInsets.ime.getBottom(density), so it re-requests on every keyboard height change. Fixes every screen and dialog using the component.

error_message: The keyboard's Next key did nothing; focus stayed on the current field
root_cause: KeyboardActions(onNext = { onImeAction?.invoke() }) supplies a non-null handler, which replaces Compose's default focus-advance even when onImeAction is null and the body does nothing. Every field except the last one has no onImeAction.
fix: Built `imeActionHandler` only when onImeAction != null and passed it (or null) to onDone/onGo/onNext, so the platform default applies where there is no submit action.

error_message: AnfasDialog KDoc claimed 'a scrollable body' but the body Column had no verticalScroll; a tall form pushed its own footer (Save/Cancel) off the bottom edge
root_cause: The body Column was unbounded and unscrollable, so with a keyboard-shrunk window the six form dialogs could be neither submitted nor dismissed. The component's own documentation asserted otherwise.
fix: Body Column now has weight(1f, fill = false) + verticalScroll, and the dialog has imePadding(). Extracted AnfasDialogPanel (internal) because Dialog opens its own window and ignores composing constraints, making the invariant untestable via the public composable; pinned by AnfasDialogTest, verified to fail when the fix is reverted.

error_message: Self-inflicted: changed App.kt from safeDrawing to systemBars.union(displayCutout) on the theory that safeDrawing's IME component was being consumed, with a comment asserting it fixed the bug. It changed nothing.
root_cause: Diagnosed by reasoning instead of measurement. windowInsetsPadding(x.only(sides)) limits its consumption to the sides it pads, so the bottom/IME inset was never consumed. A temporary debug Text printing WindowInsets.ime.getBottom() showed ime=1008 and the layout clipping at exactly screen-1008, proving imePadding was already working.
fix: Reverted App.kt entirely. Measure the inset before editing layout code on a consumption hunch.

error_message: A restored/transferred install showed the dashboard as an authenticated user whose staff row did not exist; also a demoted staff member kept their old permissions until sign-out
root_cause: observeSession() returned sessionStore.observe() verbatim, so the session was whatever key-value storage held. Settings survives backup and device transfer while the Room file is deliberately excluded (PII), so an install can hold a session id for a row that does not exist. The stored role set was also a snapshot from sign-in time, so role changes did not take effect until sign-out.
fix: observeSession() now flatMapLatest's into dao.observeById(storedId) and emits null when the row is absent, disabled, or resolves no role; roles are taken from the row. 5 tests added, 4 of which fail when the fix is reverted. Reproduced and verified on the emulator by seeding shared_prefs with a session and no databases dir: before = dashboard, after = 'Set up this device'.

error_message: Concluded a correct fix had failed on device; had actually side-loaded a day-old APK
root_cause: AGP 9 writes the debug APK to build/intermediates/apk/debug/. The legacy build/outputs/apk/debug/ path still held an artifact from the previous day, and `assembleDebug` reported success without touching it, so `adb install` of that path installed stale code.
fix: Installed from build/intermediates/apk/debug/. Check the APK mtime against the source before drawing a conclusion from a device run.

error_message: e: AuthRepositoryTest.kt:349:9 Name contains illegal characters: ",".
root_cause: A backtick test name containing a comma. Kotlin/Native rejects it; only compileTestKotlinIosSimulatorArm64 surfaces it, so the JVM tests passed first. Third occurrence of an already-documented rule (see bug-069).
fix: Renamed to `roles come from the staff row rather than the stored session`. Run ./gradlew check (not just jvmTest) before shipping.

error_message: CI's push trigger listed hardening/** , which matches no branch since the per-feature naming convention (feat/fix/test) was adopted
root_cause: The pattern was written when all work happened on hardening/* branches. After switching to one descriptively-named branch per feature it silently matched nothing, so pushes to working branches ran no CI at all.
fix: Narrowed push to `main` only, with a comment explaining why the feat/fix/test patterns are deliberately NOT added (they would double-run the matrix for any branch with an open PR, and the PR run is what gates a merge).

error_message: The reminder queue was unreachable on a phone whenever it was empty
root_cause: Reminders are Placement.WideOnly, so on a phone the queue is only reachable from a parent screen. That parent was the dashboard's failed-reminders tile, whose onClick was gated on `failedReminders > 0` -- so with nothing failed (which is the normal state, and always the state before anything has been queued) there was no route at all. CLAUDE.md already claimed the 'needs renewal' tile was the route; it was not.
fix: The needing-renewal tile is now unconditionally clickable and opens the queue; the failed tile keeps its gate as a shortcut into failures. Added DashboardComponent.onOpenRemindersClicked. Found by trying to reach the new Build queue button on a device.

error_message: New ReminderQueueComponent tests failed: the scheduler was never called and no notice appeared
root_cause: onBuildQueue guards on state.value.mayBuildQueue, but state is stateIn(WhileSubscribed) -- with no collector, state.value is the initialValue where the permission is false, so the guard refused. The tests read state.value instead of subscribing.
fix: Subscribe with Turbine and drain to a settled frame before acting, matching the suite's existing pattern; added an awaitSettled helper. Note the guard fails safe (refuses rather than permits), so this was a test defect, not a production one.

error_message: PhoneE164Test > a foreign country code is preserved FAILED -- 966501234567 became 20966501234567
root_cause: The else branch prepended the default country code to any number without a leading 0 or 00, so every already-international foreign number got 20 stuck on the front. A member with a Saudi or Emirati number would have had their renewal notice sent to whoever owns the resulting Egyptian number.
fix: Use length to tell the cases apart: <=10 digits is a bare national subscriber number and gets the country code; anything longer already carries one. Prefix alone cannot distinguish them.

error_message: The reminder queue's empty state claimed 'Reminders appear here once the daily job schedules them' -- there is no daily job
root_cause: Copy written when the queue could never be populated, so nobody had read it against reality. Phase 1 made the queue real and the sentence became false. The sent tab also said 'Delivered', which overstates SENT -- Meta accepting a message is not a delivery receipt.
fix: The queued empty state now names Build queue; the sent one says 'sent' rather than 'delivered'. Both languages. Spotted from a device screenshot, not from reading code.

error_message: The reminder queue rendered its six-column desktop table on a phone: headers squeezed to 'MEM…'/'TEM…' and the status chip wrapped to two lines (three in Arabic)
root_cause: The screen had no narrow branch -- unlike IntakeReviewScreen, which already switches to one card per row below AnfasTableMinWidth. It went unnoticed because the queue was always empty until the WhatsApp scheduler landed, so no row had ever been rendered.
fix: Added ReminderCardList/ReminderCard behind a BoxWithConstraints at the same threshold, keeping bulk selection (with a labelled select-all) and the export's error stripe. Pinned by ReminderQueueLayoutTest, falsified in both directions.

error_message: The 4dp error stripe on a failed reminder card was invisible
root_cause: fillMaxHeight() inside a wrap-content Row has no height to fill and resolves to zero. The construct was copied from the table row, which works only because that row sets its own height.
fix: Modifier.height(IntrinsicSize.Min) on the card's Row, so the stripe fills the Column's height. Spotted from a device screenshot.

error_message: In Arabic the scheduled date rendered as 'أغسطس 17 2026' instead of '17 أغسطس 2026'
root_cause: scheduledLabel() was styled dataMonoLtr in the table (and copied into the new card). That style is for Latin-only runs; a localised date carries a translated month name and its runs get reordered. Exactly the rule CLAUDE.md documents. Latent in the table since it was written -- only visible once a reminder was old enough to print an absolute date rather than 'Today'.
fix: bodyMedium for the date in both the table and the card; dataMonoLtr kept for the phone number only. Verified on device: '17 أغسطس 2026'.

error_message: An unreviewed intake sheet can vanish silently: captures were written to context.cacheDir/intake, which the OS deletes under memory pressure with no notification
root_cause: cacheDir was chosen so the OS could reclaim the space. But a captured sheet is the only copy of a member's handwritten details until the batch is imported, and there is no upload_pending state and no re-capture path -- so a cache purge loses it and the review pane just shows an empty source pane with no explanation.
fix: IntakeCaptureFiles.directory moved to context.filesDir/intake; res/xml/intake_file_paths.xml switched from <cache-path> to <files-path> (a mismatch makes FileProvider.getUriForFile throw and breaks camera capture outright); IntakeImageStore.adoptLegacyCaptures() moves any file left in cacheDir/intake and reports old->new uris so the rows naming them can be repointed.

error_message: IntakeImageStore.purgeExcept had no production caller, so an image whose batch vanished without cleanup stayed on disk forever
root_cause: purgeExcept is documented as a 'startup safety net' but nothing ran at startup that used it. Written with its callers assumed rather than wired.
fix: New IntakeHousekeeping, registered single(createdAtStart = true) in IntakeOcrModule on its own IO scope with appExceptionHandler, mirroring DataModule's plan seed. Placed in :feature:intake-ocr because it needs both the batches table and the platform file store. Needed two new DAO queries (sourceImageUris, relocateSourceImage) -- queries only, so no schema change and no migration.

error_message: A purge running before legacy adoption deletes exactly the sheets adoption exists to rescue
root_cause: An adopted file has been moved into the current directory but no row names it yet, so a keep-set built from the batches table at that moment does not include it and the purge treats it as orphaned. Also: a failed keep-set read falling through to purgeExcept(emptySet()) would delete every sheet awaiting review, because an empty keep-set and 'the database could not be read' are indistinguishable to purgeExcept.
fix: run() calls adoptRelocatedCaptures() then purgeOrphanedCaptures(), sequentially in one function rather than as two independent startup jobs. A failed sourceImageUris() read logs and SKIPS the purge. IntakeHousekeepingTest pins both, asserting the keep-set's contents rather than only the call order (the order alone still reads correct if the repoint silently failed). Falsified in two directions: reversing the calls fails exactly the 2 ordering tests; making a failed read purge everything fails exactly the 1 asymmetry test.

error_message: iOS purgeExcept was a do-nothing stub commented 'nothing writes there yet', and iOS delete had no root confinement
root_cause: The stub's comment stopped being true the day ImageSource.ios.kt started writing to Application Support/intake, so the safety net silently did not exist on iOS. Separately, delete() called removeItemAtPath on whatever the DB row said, while Android deliberately confined to its own intake directory -- tolerable for one delete, much worse once purge deletes in a loop.
fix: Implemented purgeExcept against intakeDirectory() (made internal in ImageSource.ios.kt so writer and purge cannot disagree, the same mistake Android had three copies of); added a toLocalPath() root confinement matching Android; store now takes AppDispatchers so disk work leaves the caller's thread.

error_message: core:ocr:parseAndroidMainLocalResources FAILED -- [Fatal Error] intake_file_paths.xml:9:21: The string "--" is not permitted within comments.
root_cause: The new explanatory XML comment used the project's own prose convention of '--' as an em-dash substitute (the same style used throughout CLAUDE.md and KDoc). XML forbids a literal '--' anywhere inside a comment body, so the resource parser failed the whole core:ocr module before any Kotlin compiled.
fix: Reworded the one offending sentence to use a comma instead of '--'. No behavioural change; XML/HTML comments must never carry this prose convention -- use commas or parentheses in .xml files instead.

error_message: core:data:compileTestKotlinJvm FAILED -- Class 'FakeIntakeDao' is not abstract and does not implement abstract members: sourceImageUris(), relocateSourceImage(from, to)
root_cause: IntakeDao gained two new abstract methods (sourceImageUris, relocateSourceImage) for the Stage 0 capture-storage housekeeping feature, but the commonTest in-memory fake implementing IntakeDao was not updated to match, so the whole core:data test source set failed to compile.
fix: Added both methods to FakeIntakeDao: sourceImageUris() maps non-null sourceImageUri off the in-memory batch list; relocateSourceImage(from, to) rewrites matching batches' sourceImageUri, mirroring the real UPDATE ... WHERE source_image_uri = :from.

error_message: Class 'FakeSubscriptions'/'FakeSubscriptionRepository' is not abstract and does not implement abstract member: suspend fun seedPlans(...)
root_cause: Sync Stage 1 added SubscriptionRepository.seedPlans() (insert-if-absent, used by the startup seed instead of upsertPlans) but three feature-module test fakes implementing the interface predate the change and only override upsertPlans, so their jvmTest/iosSimulatorArm64Test compilation broke -- exactly the mechanical fallout the task briefing warned about.
fix: Added a trivial override suspend fun seedPlans(plans) = AppResult.Success(Unit) to each of the three fakes, matching their existing upsertPlans stub.

error_message: MigrationFromV4Test: java.lang.AssertionError: the file should be at the current schema version expected:<12> but was:<13>
root_cause: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is a hardcoded companion constant mirroring @Database(version = ...) on AnfasDatabase, with a comment noting it must be bumped together. Sync Stage 1 bumped the schema to v13 (sync_outbox + sync_tombstones via AutoMigration(12,13)) without bumping this constant -- the third time this exact test has broken this way (v5->v6 per bug-051, now v12->v13), for a reason unconnected to what the test verifies.
fix: Bumped CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION to 13. Also tried removing the constant entirely by reading version off the @Database annotation via reflection (AnfasDatabase::class.java.getAnnotation(Database::class.java).version) -- confirmed this does NOT work: Database has SOURCE-level retention that KSP consumes and does not survive into the compiled class, so getAnnotation returns null and the call throws NullPointerException at runtime (verified by actually running the test with the reflection approach before reverting). Reverted to the hardcoded constant as the only working option; the passing run after the bump is real evidence the full v4->v13 auto-migration chain (including the new sync tables) runs correctly against a real v4 database file.
